ops.title: Before proposing to remove/change a mechanism, git-log -S its introduction and recover the incident it fixed — don't plan from current-code reading alone
ops.body:
User rejected a plan to delete cc-review's `channel.hello` handshake with: *"look at why we added it in the first place, dont just blindly change things"*.

**Why:** Current-code exploration showed nothing blocked on the hello, so deletion looked safe — but `git log -S` revealed it was the v0.12.0 fix for reviews stranded on the kill-prone Monitor path, itself layered on the v0.8.0 silent-drop incident. Deleting it would have regressed a documented incident. Mechanisms in this codebase are often incident-driven; the code alone doesn't show the failure they prevent.

**How to apply:** When a plan removes or weakens an existing mechanism (a handshake, guard, retry, state machine), run `git log --all -S '<symbol>'` in the repo (and in [[cc-interact-extraction]]'s sibling repo — history may predate the extraction), read the introducing commit messages and CHANGELOG entries, and name the original motivation in the plan's Context with a "do not regress this" note. Then design the fix so the original failure stays impossible.
